issues.location: binary interleaving injection and claimed missing output
issues.finding: Equality of binary values does not by itself imply equal digit strings. The proof needs a fixed canonical expansion convention. Under the convention using non-eventually-one expansions below one and all ones for one, the stated output 0.101010... has the preimage (1,0), so it does not demonstrate failure of surjectivity.
issues.proposed_resolution: State the canonical convention and why interleaving remains canonical; use 0.001010... instead. Its odd digits force the noncanonical expansion 0.01111... of one half, while the chosen expansion is 0.1000..., so the output is missed.

issues.finding: The expansions used throughout the proof are binary, although the summary calls them decimal.

translation_treatment: The Javanese target fixes the binary-representation convention, repairs the injection justification, replaces the non-surjectivity witness, and calls the expansions binary. A bounded comparison view records the corrections; frozen English bytes remain unchanged.
